messages:
alex: Heads up — seeing a concentrated spike of Xid 48 + intermittent Xid 13 on a10 nodes in us-east-1 this morning. Started ~03:15 UTC on pool gpu-a10-mixed. Some tenants hit higher error rates and automatic drains kicked in.

maria: Which kernel/driver on those nodes? any pattern across instance sku or az?

alex: All running 525.85.12, kernel 5.15.0-70. Errors present on nodes in az us-east-1b and us-east-1c, not 1a.

jin: quick grep of logs shows Xid 48 often followed by network disconnect within 1-3s. Possibly a PCIe/host-link timeout? sample: `Xid 48: GPU context corrupted` then `link down` in host logs.

sara: Can you paste the short failure trace?

alex: ```
[2025-11-10T03:16:22Z] nvidia: Xid 48 on GPU 2: context corrupted
[2025-11-10T03:16:23Z] kernel: eth0: link down (port-change)
[2025-11-10T03:16:23Z] kubelet: Pod gpu-job-14 evicted (node condition: NetworkUnavailable)
```

kevin: Interesting — we had a host firmware upgrade roll last week only in 1b/1c. Could be a new PCIe rescan behavior. Any ECC counters incrementing?

alex: ECC counters are flat, no persistent ECC errors. `nvidia-smi -q` returns normal ECC stats. This looks different than classic ECC-bit flips.

maria: Do we also see correlated workload types (fp16/mixed-precision) or specific models?

jin: Cross-referenced X-ray logs with job metadata: 85% of affected pods were mixed-precision decoder workloads (batching heavy, kv-cache warm). Lower-rate RAG embedding jobs mostly unaffected.

sara: Could be memory allocator stress with frequent KV cache eviction + host NIC interrupts. Any driver logs about failed page pinning?

alex: Found repeated `failed to pin pages (ENOMEM)` in dmesg on one host within same window. Not on all hosts though.

kevin: Ops question — are these nodes hitting network egress quotas or oversubscription? Could trigger host pathologies if NIC performance tanked.

maria: Also check GPU clock throttling timestamps. If power/thermal throttling plus heavy network interrupts we can see context corruption.

jin: Short checklist I ran: `kubectl describe node` (no OOM), `nvidia-smi -q` (ECC ok), `dmesg | grep -i pin` (some ENOMEM), `ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "rx_errors|tx_errors"` (spikes on affected hosts).

alex: Temporary mitigation applied: set node annotation to avoid scheduling large-batch mixed-precision jobs and soft-drain 3 of the worst nodes. Observed drop in Xid 48 after soft-drain.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled canary firmware rollback to previous host image in us-east-1b at 04:10 UTC.

kevin: Good. Next steps: 1) replicate in lab with same driver + firmware + similar NIC load; 2) run mempin stress with mixed-precision workload to try to reproduce ENOMEM -> Xid 48; 3) gather NIC error counters and PCIe AER logs.

maria: I'll spin up a reproduce cluster and run the KV-heavy decoder job with `--batch 64 --fp16` and monitor `dmesg`, `ethtool`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,clocks.sm --format=csv -l 1`.

jin: If reproduce succeeds, we should try driver 535.x in lab (newer) and also test rollback to previous firmware.

alex: Also noting cost/impact: about 4% of capacity in that pool was soft-drained for ~45m, ~3 customer retries. Ops estimated ~0.6% throughput loss overall for us-east-1.

kevin: Add a post-incident note for capacity: consider increasing grace capacity in us-east-1 for mixed workloads until we root cause.

maria: I'll attach reproduce logs here when ready and tag infra-announce if we decide a broader remediation is needed.

alex: Thanks — leaving this thread pinned until we have lab repro or stacktrace. :thumbsup:
